questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

Mahesh said to the interviewer, "Sir, I was in charge of the production unit at my previous office."

options.text: Mahesh told the interviewer that Sir was in charge of the production unit at my previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer that he had been in charge of the production unit at his previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer you were in charge of the production unit at my previous office.
Mahesh told the interviewer I was in charge of the production unit at his previous office.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. Mahesh told the interviewer that he had been in charge of the production unit at his previous office.**

__
 
• While changing direct speech into indirect speech** said to** is changed into **told**.
 
• And** 'I'** is referred to **Mahesh**, hence, 'I' will be changed into **'he'**.
 
• The tense of the reported speech (here:** Simple past)** would undergo a** backshift **(get changed into** Past perfect) i.e. 'was/were'** would be changed into **'had been' **and** V2 would be changed into V3.**
 
• All these rules are followed in option 2, hence, it will be the correct answer.

NOTE: __When a sentence is converted from Direct speech into Indirect speech:

 
• If the 'reporting verb' is in 'Past tense', the 'Reported speech' would undergo a backshift of tense.
 
• Modal verbs (Will, may, can) would take their past forms (would, might, could).
 
• Pronouns would change according to the subject of reporting verb.​
 
• "said to" will get converted to "told", "asked", "commanded", requested" etc.depending on the tone of the narrator.

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The cyclone has damaged several crops.

options.text: Several crops have damaged the cyclone.

Several crops are being damaged by the cyclone
Several crops have been damaged by the cyclone.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. Several crops have been damaged by the cyclone.**

 
• The given sentence is in the** present perfect tense**, hence, while converting it into passive voice** 'has/have been' **will be used.
 
• The subject while making the passive voice will be** 'several crops'** which is a plural subject.
 
• Hence, '**have been'** will be used.
 
• In passive voice, **v3** is used.
 
• All these rules are followed in option 4), hence, it is the correct answer.

questions.solution:

questions.question:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct?

8 + 15 - 20 × 10 ÷ 5 = 47
questions.solution:
8 + 15 - 20 × 10 ÷ 5 = 47

Interchanging + and -, 8 and 15

15 - 8 + 20 × 10 ÷ 5 (according to BODMAS rule)

= 15 - 8 + 20 × 2

= 15 – 8 + 40

= 55 - 8

= 47

Hence, the correct answer is + and -, 8 and 15.

questions.question: What was the day of the week on 26 January 2012?
questions.solution:
Number of odd days till 2011 = no. of odd days in 2000 years (century leap year) + no. of odd days from 2001 to 2011 = 0 odd days + (11 odd days + 2 odd days (as there are 2 leap years)) = remainder of 13 ÷ 7 = 6

Number of odd days up to 26 January 2012 = remainder of 26 ÷ 7 = 5

Total odd days = 5 + 6 = 11 = remainder of 11 ÷ 7 = 4.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statement:**

No carrot is roof.

All roofs are potatoes.

**Conclusions:**

I. No carrot is potatoes.

II. No potatoes is carrot.

III. Some potatoes are roofs.

IV. All the potatoes are roofs.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48e0f7271543cba7c440e46fc0011240882d91d383d88c2db141f5d3ecf1d288.png] 

**Explanation:**

I. No carrot is potatoes - False (it is possible but not definite)

II. No potatoes is carrot. – False (it is possible but not definite)

III. Some potatoes are roofs. – True (all roofs are potatoes)

IV. All the potatoes are roofs. – False (it is possible but not definite)

Hence, only conclusion III follows.

questions.question: The average of a series of 21 numbers is equal to 43. The average of the first eleven of them is 33. The average of the last eleven numbers is 53. The eleventh number of the series is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of 21 numbers is = 43

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of terms/number of terms

**Calculation:**

Sum of 21 numbers = 43 × 21 = 903

Sum of first 11 numbers = 33 × 11 = 363

Sum of last 11 numbers = 53 × 11 = 583

The eleventh number = 363 + 583 – 903 = 43

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 20 hours. Both the pipes are opened at 6.30 a.m. When will the tank get filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An inlet pipe can fill the tank in 10 hours

An outlet pipe can empty the tank in 20 hours

Both pipes are opened at 6.30 a.m

**Formula used:**

Work done = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let the capacity of the tank be 20 units.

(∵ LCM of 10 and 20 is 20)

Efficiency of inlet pipe = 20/10 = 2

Efficiency of outlet pipe = -20/20 = -1

1 hour work of both pipe = 2 – 1 = 1

Time taken to filled the tank = 20/1 = 20 hours

Time = 6.30 am + 20 = 2.30 a.m. next day

**∴ The tank will be filled by 2.30 a.m next day**

questions.question: The 10-digit number 79x00001y6 is exactly divisible by 88. What is the value of (x + y)?
questions.solution:
For the divisible by 88 it will be also divisible by 11 and 8.

For the divisible by 11, difference of sum of alternate digit of a number should be zero.

⇒ (7 + x + 0 + 0 + y) ∼ (9 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 6) = 0

⇒ x + y + 7 = 16

⇒ x + y = 9

For the divisible by 8, last three digits of a number are divisible by 8.

⇒ y = 3, 7

∵ x + y = 9

When y = 3 ⇒ x = 6

When y = 7 ⇒ x = 2

⇒ x + y = 6 + 3 = 2 + 7 = 9

questions.question: A train goes from P to Q with a speed u km/h, then from Q to R (QR = 2PQ) with a speed 3u km/h, and returns from R to P With a speed u/2 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the train for the entire journey starting from P and back to P?
questions.solution:
Let the distance between P to Q be d.

⇒ QR = 2d

⇒ RP = 3d

Average speed = total distance/total time

Total time = distance/speed

Time taken by train from P to Q = d/u

Time taken by train from Q to R = 2d/3u

Time taken by train from R to P = 3d/(u/2) = 6d/u

Total time = d/u + 2d/3u + 6d/u = 23d/3u

Total distance = d + 2d + 3d = 6d

Average speed = 6d/(23d/3u) = 18u/23

questions.question: The famous Madhubani artist who won the Bihar Ratna in 1984 is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sita Devi__.**

 
• Sita Devi was one of the most prominent early Mithila artists.
 
• She was among the first to transfer the traditional art form from the walls of the home to paper and canvas from the village of **Jitwarpur, Bihar**.
 
• She popularized the** ‘Bharni’ style** of Mithila painting, which emphasizes strong colours over fine lines.
 
• In **1975**, she won a **National Award.**
 
• In **1981 **she was awarded the** Padma Shri**, one of India’s highest civilian honours.
 
• In **1984** won the **Bihar Ratna Samman**.
 
• During her career, she exhibited her work in more than ten countries.
 
• Her art is present in the permanent collections of the Victoria & Albert Museum in London, the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the Musée du Quai Branly in Paris, the** Mithila Museum in Japan** and many other international institutions.
 
• **Madhubani painting** is one of the many famous Indian art forms.
 
• As it is practised in the Mithila region of Bihar and Nepal, it is called** Mithila **or Madhubani art.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a natural greenhouse gas?
questions.solution:

• Gases that trap heat in the atmosphere are called **greenhouse gases. **

**Carbon dioxide (CO₂):**

 
• ​It enters the atmosphere through burning fossil fuels solid waste, trees and other biological materials.
 
• Carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere (or "sequestered") when it is absorbed by plants as part of the biological carbon cycle.

**Methane (CH4):**

 
• Methane is emitted during the production and transport of coal, natural gas, and oil.
 
• Methane emissions also result from livestock and other agricultural practices and by the decay of organic waste in municipal solid waste landfills.

**Nitrous oxide (N₂O)**:

 
• Nitrous oxide is emitted during agricultural and industrial activities, combustion of fossil fuels and solid waste, as well as during treatment of wastewater.

**Fluorinated gases: **

 
• Hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, sulfur hexafluoride, and nitrogen trifluoride are synthetic, powerful greenhouse gases that are emitted from a variety of industrial processes.

questions.question: A biochemical compound is any ________.

options.text: carbon-based compound found in living things
hydrogen-based compound found in living things
mineral-based compound found in living things
sulfur-based compound found in living things

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. ​__carbon-based compound found in living things__.**

 
• The compounds found in** living things** are known as **biochemical compounds.**
 
• Biochemical compounds make up the cells and other structures of organisms and carry out life processes.
 
• **Carbon** is the basis of all biochemical compounds, so carbon is essential to life on Earth.
 
• The reason is carbon’s ability to form stable bonds with many elements, including itself. This property allows carbon to form a huge variety of very large and complex molecules.
 
• The vast number of biochemical compounds can be grouped into just **four major classes**: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.

questions.question: The right pulmonary artery is ______.

options.text: of same size as the left

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __longer than the left__.**

 
• The** right pulmonary artery **is the** longer of the two**.
 
• It passes transversely across the midline in the upper chest and passes below the aortic arch to enter the hilum of the right lung as part of its root.
 
• The** left pulmonary artery **is the** shorter **of the two terminal branches of the pulmonary trunk.
 
• It pierces the pericardium (the sac around the heart) and enters the hilum of the left lung.
 
• These arteries then deliver **oxygen-depleted blood **to each corresponding lung.
 
• This is one of the rare arteries that carry deoxygenated blood.

questions.question: Which of the following is the major state taxes in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. __Stamp duty and registration__.**

__
 
• Stamp duty and registration__ is levied by state governments on documents used in transactions such as contracts, mortgages, licences and commissions.
 
• Stamp duty is levied on documents that create, transfer, limit, extend, extinguish or record a right or liability.
 
• Such documents become legal when they are stamped with either **adhesive or embossed stamps**, and after the duty is paid in full.
 
• It is the responsibility of the writer or bearer of the document to pay the stamp tax to the government officials or other officials.
 
• These individuals will often include the stamp tax in their service fees.

questions.question: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. __​23 March 1931__.**

 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a socialist revolutionary and freedom fighter who was executed at the age of 23 for his dramatic violence against the British rule.
 
• On **March 23, 1931**, Bhagat Singh along with his associates **Sukhdev Thapar and Shivaram Rajguru** were hanged to death for the assassination of 21-year-old British police officer John Saunders. 
 
• The day they were executed is celebrated as **Martyrs' Day** throughout the country.
